name: atr_channel_breakout_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: When NIFTY closes above its 2-minute ATR-adaptive Keltner Channel (EMA_24 + 2×ATR_24) with above-average volume on a 5-second bar, passive sell-side liquidity at that level has been fully absorbed by active institutional buyers. On NIFTY, these breakouts trigger momentum-following algorithms and delta-hedging from option market makers within seconds, producing a 10-20 spot point continuation impulse in the first 30-90 seconds. The ATR-adaptive channel ensures the breakout exceeds current intraday volatility noise, distinguishing genuine institutional flow from routine price oscillation around the channel midline. Low-VIX filter (VIX < 22) excludes stress regimes where breakouts reverse violently due to gap risk.

indicators.name: ema_24
indicators.purpose: Keltner channel midline and trigger baseline. 24 bars = 2 minutes at 5s resolution. Original used EMA(20) on 1-min bars (20 min context); compressed to 2 minutes because we hold 30-90s and need a midline that reflects the current short-term price center, not a 20-minute trend. A 2-minute EMA is responsive enough to define the intraday micro-channel while filtering sub-30s noise.

indicators.name: atr_24
indicators.purpose: Adaptive channel width based on current NIFTY volatility. 24 bars matches EMA lookback for channel consistency. Original used ATR(20) on 1-min bars (20 min ATR); at 5s bars, a 2-minute ATR captures the current session volatility regime within the same conceptual window as the channel midline — when NIFTY is choppy, the channel widens and fewer breakouts fire, which is the intended behavior.

indicators.name: kc_upper
indicators.purpose: Upper channel boundary. Price closing above this on a 5-second bar means the spot move has exceeded the current 2-minute ATR band — a statistically meaningful move for the institutional flow thesis.

indicators.name: kc_lower
indicators.purpose: Lower channel boundary for bearish breakout detection.

indicators.name: vol_sma_12
indicators.purpose: 1-minute volume baseline (12 bars × 5s). Original used SMA(volume, 20) on 1-min bars (20-min baseline). Compressed to 1 minute because intraday NIFTY volume has strong time-of-day seasonality; a 1-minute baseline adapts faster to session rhythms than a 20-minute window, giving a more accurate 'normal' volume level for the current moment.

indicators.name: rel_volume
indicators.purpose: Relative volume ratio for confirming breakout is backed by real institutional participation, not a thin-market spike.

conditions: rel_volume > vol_ratio_threshold (above-average volume on breakout bar)
buy_ce.confirmation: 5-second bar closes above upper Keltner Channel with elevated volume

conditions: rel_volume > vol_ratio_threshold (above-average volume on breakout bar)
buy_pe.confirmation: 5-second bar closes below lower Keltner Channel with elevated volume

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points (~8 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5). A genuine Keltner Channel breakout should not retrace back inside the channel within 30s — 8 spot points is roughly the half-width of the ATR channel during normal sessions, so a stop at 4 option points means 'the breakout was fake and price re-entered the channel.' Consistent with typical 30s NIFTY moves of 2-5 option points: we give one full range of noise before stopping out.
exit.target_rationale: 7 option points (~14 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5). Confirmed NIFTY Keltner breakouts with volume typically extend 15-25 spot points beyond the channel before first pullback as momentum algorithms amplify the move in the 60-90s window. At 14 spot points we capture ~60% of the median move at a 1:1.75 stop-to-target ratio, which is profitable at 48%+ win rate.

filters.vix_filter: vix_close < 22.0 (default) — avoids volatile regimes where breakouts reverse due to macro shock risk
filters.time_filter: 09:25-15:20 IST — skip first 10 min (opening auction noise) and last 10 min (end-of-day unwind)
filters.volume_filter: rel_volume > 1.5 — breakout bar must have 1.5x normal 1-minute volume to confirm institutional participation
filters.trend_filter: none — channel breakout is self-defining direction
filters.spread_filter: limit order execution, no spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — ATR-adaptive channels self-adjust to regime changes; mechanism depends on institutional momentum flow which is structurally persistent on NIFTY

adaptation_notes: Original held 15-45 minutes on 1-min FnO stock bars. Compressed to 30-90 second NIFTY holds on 5-second bars. Key changes: (1) EMA/ATR lookback compressed from 20 min to 2 min — we're catching the immediate breakout impulse, not the multi-minute trend; (2) volume baseline compressed from 20 min to 1 min — adapts to intraday volume rhythm faster; (3) removed VWAP filter (original required close > VWAP) — on NIFTY, intraday momentum can break the channel both above and below VWAP legitimately; (4) removed ATR-based stop (stop at EMA midline) — replaced with fixed option premium points since ATR doesn't apply to option prices; (5) reduced max trades from 5 to 6 (more signals expected at 5-second frequency but capped for risk management); (6) session start moved to 09:25 to skip 10 min of opening noise.
weaknesses: At 5-second resolution, many false breakout bars will exceed the channel briefly and reverse — volume filter may not be sufficient to distinguish true breakouts from spikes
NIFTY channel at 2-minute ATR scale may fire too frequently during trending sessions — max_trades_per_day cap important
Volume data quality at 5-second frequency varies; thin bars near session open/close can generate misleading rel_volume spikes
Low-VIX filter (< 22) means strategy is inactive during exactly the conditions when NIFTY makes its largest moves
